headline: Corn's 4.1% WASDE drop closes out a mixed week
lead: Corn settled Friday at $4.80, down 4.1% after WASDE came in heavier than the trade wanted. Cattle shrugged it off, closing the week at $224.60, up 1.2%, with feeders up 1.7% to $343.90. Every bushel of old-crop corn sitting in the bin is worth about 19 cents less than it was Thursday.
teaser: Corn fell almost 4% on WASDE Friday while cattle and feeders closed the week higher.

one_number.unit: USDA CRP and Grassland CRP payments issued
one_number.context: USDA cut checks to producers idling land for conservation, real cash into farm country even as corn took its worst day in weeks.

sections.title: Corn takes the brunt of wasde
sections.body:
- Corn settled Friday at **$4.80**, down 3.9% on the day after Friday's WASDE report.
- Winter wheat took a hit too, with Chicago wheat easing to $6.71, down 1.8% on the week's close.
- World Grain reports US grain storage is more available this year, which should ease the bin-space squeeze farmers faced at harvest.
sections.so_what: Heavier supply numbers plus easier storage both point the same direction: less urgency to move.

sections.title: Cattle and feeders close the week firm
sections.body:
- Live cattle closed at **$224.60**, up 1.2% Friday, with feeders up 1.7% to $343.90.
- Both held their gains even as corn, the main feed cost, dropped 4.1% the same session.
- Hogs went the other way, down 0.9% to $75.15, still sitting near the bottom of its 52-week range.
sections.so_what: Cheaper corn into a strong cattle market is good margin math for anyone feeding out.

sections.title: Diesel politics move to the front
sections.body:
- Crude held near flat Friday at **$91.69**, up only 0.2%, even with tanker rates at record highs tied to the Iran-Hormuz cycle, a re-escalation since July that has mostly cooled since.
- Trump said he discussed buying Russian diesel with Putin, with the stated goal of bringing diesel prices down.
sections.so_what: Diesel, not crude, has been the real input-cost story heading into fall fieldwork and now.

outside_the_pit.title: USDA issues $1.8 billion in CRP payments
outside_the_pit.body: The payments went out late Thursday to producers idling land under CRP and Grassland CRP, real dollars into farm country this week.

watch_list.desc: Crop Progress report. Watch for harvest pace after corn's hard drop Friday.
Corn below $4.80 again next week would say the WASDE number is still being digested.
Diesel price moves tied to any US-Russia purchase deal could shift fall fieldwork costs.

source_summary: CME settlement data, USDA WASDE, USDA CRP announcement, oilprice.com, feedstuffs.com, world-grain.com, thefencepost.com
